- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -1.0) or shows recent volatility, model often underestimates or lags; adjust upward by 1–3% if price is trending up.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.0), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; align forecast toward 3–5-day moving average of recent prices.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the forecast window; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for first 7–10 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment spikes, model underreacts; increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment shifts by 10–20% for next 3 days.
